concepts.title: Simple Present Tense: Fill the Blank
concepts.definition: The simple present tense states habits, routines and general truths. With he, she, it or one person or thing, the verb takes -s or -es; with I, you, we, they the base verb is used.
concepts.key_idea: Third person singular is the only subject that changes the verb.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with the simple present form of the verb in brackets
Choose the correct simple present verb for the sentence
Complete the sentence in the simple present tense

solution_steps.explain: he/she/it or a singular noun takes verb + s/es
a plural subject or I/you/we/they takes the base verb
the word in brackets is the base verb; add -s/-es only for he/she/it

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with the simple present form: She ___ to school every day. (go)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: Ravi ___ cricket every evening. (play)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: My father ___ tea every morning. (drink)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: The sun ___ in the east. (rise)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: They ___ their grandmother every Sunday. (visit)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: The baby ___ sweetly. (smile)
Fill in the blank with the simple present form: This shop ___ at nine o'clock. (open)

concepts.title: Articles: a, an, the
concepts.definition: A and an introduce one singular countable noun; an comes before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. The points to one particular thing already known or named.
concepts.formula: an + vowel sound;  a + consonant sound;  the + specific noun
concepts.key_idea: It is the sound, not the letter, that decides a or an.
question_patterns: Fill in the blank with a, an or the
Choose the correct article for the sentence
Complete the sentence with the right article

solution_steps.explain: does it begin with a vowel sound? use an; otherwise use a
if the sentence names one particular thing, use the
one singular countable noun first mentioned takes a or an

worked_examples.q: Fill in the blank with a, an or the: I saw ___ elephant at the zoo.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: Ria ate ___ apple during the break.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: Vikram is ___ honest boy.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: My mother is ___ doctor.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: Please pass me ___ salt kept here.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: We stayed at ___ hotel near the station.
Fill in the blank with a, an or the: ___ Yamuna flows through Delhi.

concepts.title: Plurals: Write the Plural Form
concepts.definition: Most nouns form the plural by adding -s. Nouns ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x or -o add -es; nouns ending in a consonant + y change y to ies; some nouns change inside (child to children).
concepts.key_idea: Spelling rules, not meaning, build the plural form.
question_patterns: Write the plural form of the given noun
Give the plural of the word
Change the noun into its plural form

solution_steps.explain: child, tooth, mouse, man, foot change inside
